chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

That a man came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said: 'May Allah improve you, we trade in these mountains and find places there where we cannot pray except on the snow.' He said: 'Would you not be content to be like so-and-so, who is content with less?' Then he said: 'Do not seek trade in a land where you cannot pray except on the snow.'

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir), a key Shia Imam

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on trading in places where one cannot perform prayer properly?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) addresses the practical dilemma of merchants in remote mountainous regions where limited space forces them to pray on snow. He uses a rhetorical question to highlight the spiritual cost of such compromise, ultimately advising that one should not seek trade in places where proper prayer (*salah*) becomes unduly difficult, thereby prioritizing the preservation of worship over commercial gain. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of removing hardship (*raf' al-haraj*) in religious obligations, even within the context of permissible trade.
